correctness.rationale: In the repaired proof, length additivity in w=uv holds also with v replaced by vs for s∈J. Thus the right descents in J are exactly those of v, and the unnormalized character sum is the parabolic Eulerian value multiplied by the index. Components give a product and longest-element complementarity kills odd ranks. Type A/B secant-tangent evaluations, the type D identity, and the dihedral calculation give nonzero even ranks: tan'=1+tan² implies odd-indexed zigzag numbers beyond E_1 are even (paired terms, with an even central binomial coefficient if unpaired), and sec'=sec·tan then implies even-indexed numbers are odd. The original H_4 evaluation 1936 came from the erroneous printed Cohen row, whose coefficients sum to 7200 instead of the group order 14400. Expanding ∏(2·1_{s is not a right descent}−1) reduces P_W(−1) to the signed weighted parabolic indices. At sizes 0 through 4 the sums for H_4 are 14400, −57600, 68160, −21120, 16 and give the corrected nonzero 3856. Exact independent parabolic arithmetic also matched F_4, E_6 and E_8. The parity-boundary bijection is valid: a tree edge set of positive odd degrees has even components; conversely pair the vertices in each even induced component and take the symmetric difference of paths, unique since no nonempty forest edge set has all degrees even. Rooting at a leaf (or the singleton) gives 0, 1, or 2 children; the absent/present-parent counts from two branches are ac+bc+ad and ac+bd, with only the permitted incident degrees. The Fibonacci addition law gives F_{s+1},F_s for s vertices; F_{r+1} counts the nonzero characters. The real Walsh basis gives both fields' ranks and the factorization for a direct product. The correction changes a real proof evaluation but does not change the support or rank theorem.
residual_risks: The frozen finite verifier checks B/D support and small trees, not the exceptional values or all ranks; the new independent computation evaluates parabolic sums on the explicitly named diagrams only. Degree at most three is essential for the universal tree count; no arbitrary-rank graph generalization or inverse norms are claimed.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Selected edge sets can be turned into vertex subsets of a line graph. This covers paths but not branching Coxeter trees: an induced K_{1,3} occurs at a degree-three tree vertex, whereas line graphs are claw-free. The broader results on Coxeter descent statistics do not supply the shape-independent tree count.

value.rationale: The degree-three parity count is an independently meaningful exact invariant: despite branching, the number of vertex subsets with all components even depends only on order in this natural tree class. The boundary interpretation and two-state mechanism explain why the same rank extends from path diagrams to branching finite Coxeter diagrams. The value does not rest on recomputing the classical Eulerian table or correcting one of its entries.
